children: Silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) declined by up to 2 percent on Thursday, tracking a sharp fall in international silver prices, which dropped by as much as 5 percent in the previous session amid a stronger US dollar and growing expectations of higher interest rates by the US Federal Reserve.
However, Silver prices recovered in today's session and rose 0.87 percent to Rs 1.62 lakh per kilogram in futures trade .
At around 12:50 pm, Nippon India Silver ETF was trading 1.38 percent lower, while Groww Silver ETF and Zerodha Silver ETF declined 1.31 percent and 1.46 percent, respectively.
Tata Silver ETF fell 1.39 percent, while ICICI Prudential Silver ETF was down 1.81 percent.
Shares of Hindustan Zinc, the country's largest silver producer, were trading 1.45 percent lower at Rs 519.35 per share.
Silver prices witnessed a sharp sell-off in the previous session. On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), silver futures for December delivery slumped Rs 5,872, or 3.46 percent, to Rs 1,63,830 per kg.

"Bullion faces a double headwind as international prices are falling because of the stronger dollar, while the stronger rupee reduces domestic prices further," said Anindya Banerjee, Head of Commodity and Currency Research at brokerage firm Kotak Neo.
The weakness was also visible in overseas markets, where Comex silver futures for December delivery fell more than 3 per cent to USD 45.79 per ounce.

"Silver slipped below USD 46 per ounce in global trade, falling to its lowest level in more than a year due to a firm US dollar and growing expectations of higher interest rates by the Federal Reserve, which kept pressure on bullion," said Renisha Chainani, Chief Research Officer at Augmont, an integrated gold and silver platform.

Meanwhile, some recovery was seen during Thursday's session. On the Multi Commodity Exchange, the white metal futures for December delivery jumped Rs 1,402, or 0.87 percent to Rs 1,62,136 per kg in a business turnover of 16,463 lots.
In overseas trade, Comex silver futures for December also advanced by 0.71 percent to USD 45.378 per ounce.

title: Silver ETFs decline up to 2%, Hindustan Zinc shares down as precious metal crashes up to 5%
